title: burst-aware-block-allocator-and-eviction-scheduler-to-reduce-kv-cache-tail-latency
author: Ethan Zhang
release_notes: Add burst-aware transient reservation to paged KV block allocator and a cooperative eviction scheduler that preserves batch hotpaths; reduces 95th/99th tail latency under bursty request patterns. No API changes; runtime flags for tuning.
commits: add: burst sensor and transient_reserve counters
refactor: allocator free path instrumentation and metrics
test: unit + integration + bench harness for burst scenarios
docs: allocator design notes and tuning guidance
description:
Motivation: We see recurring tail-latency spikes in production when short-lived bursts (traffic spikes or long-tail model calls) coincide with KV cache reclamation work. Current paged KV allocator does not distinguish transient bursts from steady-state pressure: it starts aggressive eviction on detection of low free blocks and sometimes runs eviction work on the hot path which lengthens batch latencies. This PR introduces a burst-aware transient reservation and a cooperative eviction scheduler that defers/pauses reclamation during latency-sensitive windows and performs targeted background reclaiming when the runtime signals quieter windows (e.g., between batching flushes).

Implementation summary: Single continuous string below to preserve GitHub PR body style. We add a lightweight burst sensor (kv::BurstSensor) that tracks allocation rate and detects short-lived spikes by maintaining short sliding windows of allocation events and recent batch completion markers. The block allocator now exposes a transient_reserve counter: when a burst is detected we reserve a small headroom of blocks per-pool to avoid immediate eviction. Eviction work is moved out of synchronous allocation slow-path into eviction_scheduler, a cooperative component that subscribes to runtime batching events via a new low-overhead hook in continuous_batching (on_batch_flush/on_batch_idle). The scheduler runs reclamation tasks only when signaled idle or when free memory drops below a critical hysteresis threshold; it also accepts per-pool eviction hints (victim_ranges) from the allocator to focus work and minimize scanning.

Key behavioral changes:
- Allocator fast-path remains lock-free for common-case allocations.
- On allocation pressure, instead of immediately walking long freelists and evicting multiple pages, allocator first consults transient_reserve and attempts local reuse strategies (LRU-like local candidate reuse) up to the reserve.
- Eviction work that requires I/O or heavy compaction is enqueued to eviction_scheduler which respects a latency fence: if batch hotpath is active, eviction is throttled or paused for tunable window_ms.
- Scheduler uses per-thread backoff counters and prioritizes small, high-impact evictions (sparse victims) to recover capacity quickly with minimal cache churn.

Performance: Benchmarks in benches/kv/burst_bench.rs show the following on a 8-GPU host with representative Llama-derived model workloads and a synthetic burst pattern (1000 rps steady, 5x bursts for 2s every 20s): - 95th latency reduced by ~28% compared to main with the previous allocator strategy. - 99th latency reduced by ~41% during bursts. - End-to-end throughput unchanged or slightly improved due to fewer batch stalls. Microbenchmarks: background eviction CPU utilization dropped 33% by focusing work and avoiding full-scan passes.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for allocator behavior and BurstSensor (tests/kv/burst_allocator_test.rs) cover reserve logic and corner cases. Integration tests wire eviction_scheduler into continuous_batching simulation; CI included a simulated burst scenario (integration-kv) that was flaky initially due to a race which is fixed in commit 3. Benchmarks run on perf-lab and results attached in PR artifacts. We also ran a staged rollout to a subset of dedicated clusters: no regression signals; observability dashboards updated to show burst events and scheduler decisions.

Operational / rollout notes: New runtime flags (config/runtime_flags.toml documented and ops examples provided) allow teams to tune reserve size, detection window, and eviction_fence_ms. Defaults were chosen conservative to avoid regressions. The feature is guarded behind a runtime flag (kv.burst_reserve.enabled=true) and can be disabled at boot if needed. No schema changes; no model-serving API changes.

Review conversation summary:
- Maya: requested clarifications on reserve sizing algorithm and impact on long-lived high-pressure workloads; asked for config knobs and autoscaling guidance. Response: added reserve sizing doc and autoscaling note; default reserve is a small fraction (0.5-2% of pool) with adaptive decay.
- Priya: suggested to add metrics for "eviction_deferred_during_batch" and a histogram for eviction latency; addressed by adding eviction_{deferred,count} metrics and histograms in src/kv/metrics.rs.
- Liam: flagged a potential race between scheduler shutdown and allocator teardown in hot-swap flows; fixed by adding a graceful cancellation token and unit test.
- Reviewers approved after second pass; CI green on merge.

CI: build: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-kv: flaky on first run (race reproduction) -> fixed -> rerun -> pass; bench pipeline: artifacts uploaded (perf/burst_run_2026-03-01). Final ci_status: pass.

Merge: squashed merge; commit message: "burst-aware block allocator + eviction scheduler: reduce KV cache tail latency under bursts". Rollout: enabled on canary dedicated clusters for 72 hours and then global rollout.
